article.title: NFL EDGE Monday Morning Brief
article.dek: Week 10 ends tonight with one game: the Chargers visit the Ravens, Baltimore is the only card on the board, and the final injury names land about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Lead: One game left in Week 10 — and one card on it
paragraphs: Sunday night is settled. Cincinnati beat Pittsburgh 38-18 behind Joe Burrow's 409 yards and four touchdowns, and the Bengals take first place in the AFC North.

That leaves one game in Week 10: the Chargers at the Ravens tonight, 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff at M&T Bank Stadium. The board has one live card on it — Hit Rate, on Baltimore's moneyline. Balanced and Value have no play tonight. The app found nothing plus-EV.

items.headline: Injuries: McConkey is out, Brissett starts, and five Chargers names are still open
paragraphs: Ladd McConkey is out. The Chargers downgraded him from questionable on Sunday — back injury, missed practice all week, not traveling to Baltimore.

Five more Chargers are questionable: tight end David Njoku (fibula), linebacker Denzel Perryman (pectoral), linemen Trey Pipkins III and Kayode Awosika, and defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe. Justin Herbert is listed as probable with a finger injury.

For Baltimore, Lamar Jackson is out with a thumb injury and Tyler Huntley is out too, so Jacoby Brissett starts. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins is out with a knee injury, and running back Adam Randall is questionable.
The final inactive lists come out about 90 minutes before kickoff. That is when the five questionable names get decided.

items.headline: One live card: Hit Rate on Baltimore moneyline — and what it is actually for
paragraphs: Hit Rate is Baltimore moneyline at -230 on DraftKings. That is the pick the app thinks is most likely to win tonight. It is not the value play. The app's own tutorial says it plainly: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

Say the price out loud before you touch it. At -230, every $2.30 you risk wins $1. The app rates this one LOW reliability, and its play-through is -233 — if the price drifts past that, the verdict changes.
Balanced has no play tonight, and Value has no play either. The app found nothing plus-EV on this game. A quiet card is a real answer.

items.takeaway: Hit Rate is Baltimore moneyline -230 — the likeliest winner, not a value play — and Balanced and Value are empty tonight.

items.headline: The app sees tonight's game much closer than the market does
paragraphs: The market has Baltimore -4.5. The app's expected margin is about even — basically a coin flip on the spread. That is roughly four and a half points closer than the market.

Same story on the total. The board has 38.5. The app's projection sits near 44. That is a big gap, and it is exactly the kind of thing to run through Check: type in your book's total and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
If your book is not DraftKings or FanDuel, the board's numbers are not your numbers. Check is how you get a verdict on yours.

items.headline: The quarterbacks check out — Herbert against Brissett
paragraphs: The app is pricing the right quarterbacks for tonight: Justin Herbert for the Chargers, Jacoby Brissett for the Ravens. Brissett is in because Lamar Jackson is out with a thumb injury.
That matters because a stale quarterback is how a good verdict goes bad. If a late change hits before kickoff, the old verdict is dead — Check the new number before you bet it.

items.headline: Learn the Game: play-through — the price where the answer changes
paragraphs: Play-through is the price where the app's verdict flips. Every card has one. It is the line in the sand between bet and no-bet on that pick.

Here is a clearly labeled hypothetical example. Say the app likes a team at -150, with a play-through of -170. At -150, the verdict is bet. If the price drifts to -180, the verdict flips to no-bet — same team, same game, worse price, different answer.
That is why the price matters as much as the pick. A good team at a bad price is a pass. When you see a play-through on a card, treat it as the most you should pay.
items.takeaway: Play-through is the most you should pay for a pick — past that price, the same team in the same game becomes a no-bet.

items.headline: Monday is steady at Ravens -4.5 — and Sunday night closed the way the line said it would not
paragraphs: Nothing moved overnight on tonight's game. Baltimore is still -4.5 at DraftKings and FanDuel, the total is still 38.5, and the moneyline is still Baltimore -230. The board caught all of it.

Sunday night is the one that moved and settled. Cincinnati closed at -3.5, drifted down from -4.5 during the day, and then covered it easily in the 38-18 win. The public stayed on Cincinnati while the line came toward Pittsburgh — and the favorite won by 20 anyway. A line move is a fact, not a fortune teller.
If your book's number is different from the board's, tap Check, type in your line and price, and get a verdict on your number.

items.headline: Today's job: wait only for the inactive list, then bet a good number now
paragraphs: The only thing worth waiting for today is the inactive list, about 90 minutes before kickoff. That decides the five questionable Chargers — Njoku, Perryman, Pipkins, Awosika, and Eboigbe.

After that, there is nothing left to wait for. If your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number at kickoff, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.

One more thing: settlement is manual. The tracker only works if you are honest with yourself — log the losers too. Sunday night's Balanced card lost; write it down the same way you write down the wins.
